newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Athletics - Two Kiwis top world athletic list.
newsitem.headline: Athletics - Two Kiwis top world athletic list.

text.p: WELLINGTON, May 13 - Middle distance runner Toni Hodgkinson and discus thrower Beatrice Faumuina are on top of the world in their specialist events this year, according to the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF).

The IAAF on Tuesday released its top three performances for 1997 in all events and Hodgkinson, who reached the 800 metres final at last year's Atlanta Olympic Games and was fifth in the world indoor championships 800 metres final, is credited with the first and third-best performances this year.
Hodgkinson's best time of 1min 59.42secs at the Melbourne grand prix meet in February puts her ahead of American Jearl Miles-Clark and her next best effort, 2:00.83 is third on the list.

Faumuina, who had a poor Atlanta Games where she failed to progress beyond the opening round, tops the discus list with a throw of 68.28 metres, achieved at the Australian championships in Melbourne in March.
That broke her own New Zealand record, set a new Commonwealth mark and would have given her a silver medal at the Atlanta Games.
Australian Lisa-Marie Vizanari is second at 65.86m while Faumuina also comes in third with another throw of 65.34m.
A third New Zealander, heptathlete Joanne Henry, is rated third in the multi-discipline event with a best mark of 5919 points.
American Tiffany Lott is first on the list with 6042 points.
